description: Judge one piece of menswear before someone pays for it. Use when someone asks whether a piece of men's clothing or a pair of men's shoes is worth it ("is this worth it?", "is this a good deal?", "should I buy this?"), or pastes a men's clothing or shoe listing with a price, including Nordstrom Rack, outlet, eBay and Grailed finds. Give the maker, the category and the price, plus where it is sold and, if known, the compare-at price, fiber and build from the listing. Returns a verdict (Worth it, Worth it if the tag checks out, Only at a lower price, Skip it, Pay less, or Not enough to judge when the ledger does not grade the maker for that category and the listing gives no fiber or build that the ledger can score), the maker's grade, the fair price band for that kind of seller, what to check on the tag, cost per wear, and graded makers in the same category (same grade or better when the maker is graded). Limits: menswear only; prices are US dollars from the QuarterMaster ledger of 53 makers, checked September 2026, not live store prices; no stock, size or delivery checks; no orders.

build.description: Shoe or jacket construction, if the listing says.

category.description: One of: shoes (Leather shoes), boots (Boots), sneakers (Sneakers), tailoring (Suits, jackets, trousers), shirts (Shirts), knitwear (Knitwear), outerwear (Outerwear), watches (Watches), denim (Jeans), tees (Tees and polos), chore (Chore jackets and overshirts), chinos (Chinos and cotton trousers).

compare_at.description: The "compare at" or original price on the tag, if shown.

fiber.description: Fiber content from the listing, e.g. "100% wool" or "55% polyester".

maker.description: Brand or maker name as written on the listing, e.g. "Allen Edmonds", "Levi's", "J.Crew".

price.description: Price being asked, in US dollars.

where.description: full (brand site or department store), offprice (Nordstrom Rack, TJ Maxx, Marshalls), outlet (brand outlet or factory store), grey (marketplace seller), resale (eBay, Grailed, consignment). Default full.
